config.title: Recursive TreeView

intro.title: Recursive TreeView
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a TreeView component that displays a hierarchical list of items, such as a file directory or organizational chart, using recursion. You will learn how to create a React component that calls itself to render nested children, demonstrating the core programming concept of recursion—a function that solves a lesson by calling itself with a smaller subset of the data. The main technologies involved are React components, JavaScript objects for data structures, and JSX for rendering the UI. This hands-on project will help you understand how to handle nested data efficiently and build reusable, dynamic interfaces in React.
intro.usecase: Recursive TreeView patterns are essential for displaying hierarchical data structures in modern applications. You'll find them in file explorers like VS Code's sidebar, organizational charts in HR software, nested comment threads on platforms like Reddit, and category filters in e-commerce sites. As a React developer, you'll implement these patterns when building navigation menus with expandable sub-sections, document outlines with collapsible chapters, or permission management interfaces with nested role groups. Mastering recursive components enables you to create clean, maintainable solutions for any UI that needs to represent parent-child relationships.

objectives: Implement a recursive React component to render nested tree data
Apply conditional rendering to display expand/collapse UI based on node state
Construct a click handler to toggle node expansion state
Configure component props to pass node data and event handlers through recursion
Initialize component state to track expanded/collapsed status for tree nodes
Render nested tree structures with proper indentation and visual hierarchy
Manipulate component state to control which branches are expanded or collapsed

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have React and useState available to use in your component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import React and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the TreeNode component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named TreeNode that accepts props as its parameter and returns null for now.
steps.hint: Define a function called TreeNode that takes props as an argument and returns null.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the TreeNode component here
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a TreeNode component function that accepts props and returns null.
successCriteria: A TreeNode function component is defined, it accepts props, and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a function called TreeNode that takes props and returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The TreeNode component isn't defined correctly. Create a function named TreeNode that accepts props and returns null.

steps.title: Initialize tree data structure
steps.instruction: Define a constant named 'treeData' with an object representing a tree structure. The object should have a 'name' property and a 'children' array containing nested objects with the same structure.
steps.hint: Create a JavaScript object with properties 'name' (string) and 'children' (array). Add at least one child object inside the children array.
steps.expectedOutcome: A treeData constant is defined with a nested structure that can be used as initial data for the tree view.
successCriteria: treeData is defined as a constant object with 'name' and 'children' properties, where children contains at least one nested object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure treeData has both 'name' and 'children' properties, and children contains at least one nested object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The treeData structure isn't quite right. It should be an object with 'name' and 'children' properties, where children is an array containing objects with the same structure.

steps.title: Add state for expanded nodes
steps.instruction: Inside your component, initialize a state variable named 'expandedNodes' using useState. Set its initial value to an empty array.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. The state variable should hold an array of node IDs that are currently expanded.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: state for tracking selected items
const [selectedItems, setSelectedItems] = useState([]);
steps.expectedOutcome: A state variable 'expandedNodes' is initialized with an empty array, ready to track which tree nodes are expanded.
successCriteria: The component contains a useState call that declares 'expandedNodes' state variable initialized to an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState to declare a state variable named 'expandedNodes' with an initial value of an empty array.
steps.feedbackWrong: use the useState hook to create a state variable that will track which tree nodes are expanded.

steps.title: Create toggle handler function
steps.instruction: Create a function named toggleNode that takes a nodeId parameter and toggles its expanded state in the expandedNodes array.
steps.hint: Inside your component, define a function that updates the expandedNodes state using setExpandedNodes. You can use the previous state to check if the nodeId is already expanded.
steps.expectedOutcome: A toggleNode function is defined that will handle expanding and collapsing tree nodes by updating the expandedNodes state.
successCriteria: The toggleNode function is created with a nodeId parameter and updates expandedNodes state correctly.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your toggleNode function takes a nodeId parameter and updates the expandedNodes state using setExpandedNodes.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggleNode function isn't defined correctly. It should take a nodeId parameter and update the expandedNodes state.

steps.title: Add TreeNode component markup
steps.instruction: Inside your TreeNode component, return a div element.
steps.hint: The component should return JSX. Start with a simple div.
steps.expectedOutcome: The TreeNode component now returns a div element, providing the basic structure for rendering.
successCriteria: The TreeNode component returns a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the TreeNode component returns a div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The TreeNode component should return a div element.

steps.title: Display node label and toggle button
steps.instruction: Inside the TreeNode component, add a span element to display the node's label and a button to toggle expansion. The button should show '+' when collapsed and '-' when expanded.
steps.hint: You'll need to add JSX elements inside the div that TreeNode returns. Use a span for the label text and a button with conditional text based on whether the node is expanded.
steps.expectedOutcome: The TreeNode component now displays a label and a toggle button with conditional text.
successCriteria: The TreeNode component returns a div containing a span element and a button element with conditional text based on expansion state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some elements, but make sure you have both a span for the label and a button with conditional text.
steps.feedbackWrong: The TreeNode component doesn't yet display the label and toggle button as required.

steps.title: Wire toggle button to handler
steps.instruction: Add an onClick handler to the button that calls the toggleNode function with the node's id.
steps.hint: Use the onClick attribute on the button element and pass the node id as an argument to toggleNode.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: wiring a button click to a handler
<button onClick={() => handleClick(itemId)}>Toggle</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The button will have an onClick handler that triggers the toggleNode function with the appropriate node id.
successCriteria: The button element includes an onClick attribute that calls toggleNode with the node id as an argument.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the onClick handler correctly calls toggleNode with the node id.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is not properly wired to the toggle handler. Check that you've added the onClick attribute and passed the node id.

steps.title: Add recursive rendering of child nodes
steps.instruction: Inside the TreeNode component, after the toggle button, conditionally render child TreeNode components when the node is expanded.
steps.hint: Check if the node has children and if it's expanded, then map over the children to render TreeNode components for each child.
steps.expectedOutcome: The TreeNode component now recursively renders its child nodes when expanded, creating a nested tree structure.
successCriteria: Child TreeNode components are rendered conditionally based on whether the parent node has children and is expanded.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to check both conditions: the node should have children AND be expanded before rendering child nodes.
steps.feedbackWrong: The child nodes aren't rendering correctly. Check your conditional logic and ensure you're mapping over the children array properly.

steps.title: Render the root tree component
steps.instruction: In your component's return statement, render the TreeNode component and pass the treeData as a prop.
steps.hint: Pass treeData as a prop to TreeNode, like <TreeNode node={treeData} />.
steps.expectedOutcome: The TreeNode component is rendered with the root treeData passed as a prop, completing the recursive tree view.
successCriteria: TreeNode component is rendered with treeData passed as a prop.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're rendering the TreeNode component and passing treeData as a prop.
steps.feedbackWrong: The TreeNode component isn't rendered with the treeData prop. Check that you're passing treeData to TreeNode.
